title: The Lantern Keepers of Brill Hollow
cast: Petra Lindqvist, Absalom Okafor, June Tamaki
setting: Brill Hollow, a fishing village in Nova Scotia that never lets its lanterns go dark
plot: A marine biologist rents a cottage in Brill Hollow to study a die-off of herring. The villagers insist every window keep a lantern burning from dusk to dawn, and they ration oil like it is medicine. When a storm knocks out the supply boat and the oil runs low, the village has to decide whose lantern goes out first, and the biologist realizes the dark itself is hungry.
ending: She volunteers her own lantern to save the village children. At dawn the cottage is empty except for her field notebook, now written in a handwriting that is not hers.
note: Made for Canadian TV, aired once, never released on DVD. We have the only copy we know of. Return it or we will find you.

title: Dial Tone
setting: A late-night phone-sex switchboard in a strip-mall office in Tucson
plot: An overnight switchboard operator starts getting calls on a line that was disconnected in 1971. The caller knows what she is wearing, what she ate, and which of her coworkers will be next. Every time she hangs up, the hold music changes to a song from the day one of them was born.
ending: She rips the switchboard out of the wall, but her own cell phone rings with the same hold music, and the caller ID is her own number.
note: The hold-music sting will haunt your car rides. Rewind the last ten minutes, there is a face in the window.

title: Mother of Salt
cast: Carmen Ibarra, Tobias Rehn, Lucia Ferro
setting: Abandoned salt flats and a shuttered evaporation plant in Andalusia
plot: Three sisters return to their late mother's salt plant to sell it. The workers' dormitory is full of small salt statues of people none of them recognize, and each night a new statue appears that looks a little more like one of the sisters. The local priest refuses to set foot on the flats.
ending: The youngest sister stays behind to finish their mother's work. The final shot is her sisters' car driving away with two salt statues in the back seat.
note: Spanish with subtitles. Slow, gorgeous, cruel. Pairs well with a glass of water you will suddenly need.

title: Thirteen Floors Down
cast: Rena Holloway, Sergei Patel, Big Mike Delgado
setting: A parking garage under a Manhattan office tower that has more levels going down than the blueprints show
plot: A night-shift security guard follows a wrong-way car down the ramp of a Midtown parking garage and keeps going. Level B13 does not exist on any map, but it has cars, a working elevator, and a booth attendant who has been waiting for his replacement since 1958.
ending: The guard takes the attendant's seat so a stranded family can drive up and out. The elevator dings, and a new night guard steps off on B13.
note: Shot guerrilla-style in real New York garages. You will never park underground again.

title: The Quiet Choir
setting: A boarding school for deaf children in rural Wales
plot: A new sign-language teacher at a remote boarding school notices the students signing to someone standing in the corner of the chapel. When she asks who, they all sign the same name, the name of a student who drowned in the lake forty years earlier.
ending: She learns the drowned student was trying to warn them about the headmaster. The children sign one word to the police at the end: thank you.
note: Mostly told in sign language with subtitles. Genuinely moving under the scares. Bring tissues.

title: Grubworm
plot: When the drought cracks the ground on the Gaskins family farm, something huge starts tunneling under the peanut fields, pulling cattle down through the soil. A teenage girl with a ham radio and a crop duster is the only one who believes it is following the vibrations of the well pump.
ending: She lures the worm into the dry irrigation reservoir and floods it with the last of the county's water. A tiny worm wriggles out of a peanut shell in the final shot.
note: Pure cheese, practical effects, a theme song about the worm. Party tape.

title: Little Ghost Hotel
setting: A capsule hotel in Osaka where one capsule is always booked
plot: A broke backpacker takes a night job cleaning a capsule hotel and is told never to open capsule 44. Every morning it has been slept in. When he finally peeks, he finds a guestbook with entries from every night since 1985, all signed by the same child.
ending: He signs the guestbook and the child finally checks out. The next night the manager tells a new cleaner never to open capsule 44, and the backpacker is inside.
note: Short, sad, and creepy. More heartbreak than jump scares.

title: Seventh Bell
setting: A clock-tower monastery in the Bavarian Alps
plot: A clock repairman is hired to fix the tower clock of a monastery whose monks have taken a vow never to let it strike seven. He discovers the gears are made of human bone, and every time the clock is repaired someone in the valley vanishes.
ending: He deliberately lets the bell strike seven to break the cycle. The monks vanish instead, and the valley wakes up to find the clock has no hands.
note: German, black-and-white, grainy as dirt. The bell sound design is still unmatched.
